Surah 13: Al-Ra'd [Meccan, except for "And those who disbelieve will not cease" (the verse beginning "Ya'ṣībuhum..." as cited) and "And those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger'" (the verse), or Medinan, except for "And if there were a Qur'an..." (the two verses); it has 43, 44, 45 or 46 verses]

﴿Alif. Lam. Mim. Ra.﴾ God knows best what He intends by this. ﴿Those are the verses of the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an; the genitive is in the sense of "from" (min). ﴿And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, is the subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is ﴿the truth﴾, there is no doubt in it. ﴿But most people﴾, i.e., the people of Mecca, ﴿do not believe﴾ that it is from Him, exalted is He.

﴿It is Allah who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see.﴾ That is, *al-ʿamad* (pillars) is the plural of *ʿimād* (a pillar), which is a column (*usṭuwāna*). The verse is consistent with there being no pillars at all. ﴿Then He established Himself upon the Throne﴾ in a manner befitting Him (*istiwāʾ*, "established" or "settled"). ﴿And He subjected﴾ (meaning He made subservient) ﴿the sun and the moon, each﴾ of them ﴿running﴾ in its orbit ﴿for a specified term﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿He arranges the affair﴾, meaning He decrees the matter of His dominion. ﴿He details the signs﴾, meaning He makes clear the proofs of His power, ﴿so that you﴾, O people of Makkah, ﴿may be certain of the meeting with your Lord﴾, meaning by resurrection.

And He it is who spread out the earth (بَسَطَ, basaṭa, "spread") and placed (خَلَقَ, khalaqa, "created") in it firm mountains (جِبالًا ثَوابِت) and rivers, and of all the fruits He made in it two mates, two kinds of each. He covers (يُغَطِّي) the night with its darkness over the day. Indeed in that which has been mentioned there are signs (دِلالات, indications) of His oneness, exalted is He, for a people who reflect upon the workmanship of God.

﴿And in the earth are neighbouring tracts﴾, plots of differing soils, ﴿adjoining one another﴾. Among them is good land, salty land, and land that yields little or much. This is one of the signs of His power, exalted is He. ﴿And gardens﴾, meaning orchards, ﴿of grapes and crops﴾. The word زَرْع (crops) is read with الرَّفْع (raf', the nominative) as a coordination (ʿaṭf) upon جَنَّات (gardens), and with الجَرّ (jarr, the genitive) as a coordination upon أَعْنَاب (grapes). Likewise His saying ﴿and palm trees, in pairs and single﴾. The word صِنْوَان (ṣinwān) is the plural of صِنْو (ṣinw), and these are palm trees that share one root while their branches spread apart. ﴿And single﴾ means standing alone. ﴿Watered﴾ is read with the تَاء (tā'), so that it refers to the gardens and what is in them, and with the يَاء (yā'), so that it refers to what was mentioned. ﴿With one water﴾. ﴿And We make some of them excel others in fruit﴾ is read with the نُون (nūn) and the يَاء (yā'). The word الأُكُل (the fruit) is read with a ḍammah or a sukūn on the kāf. So some are sweet and some are sour. This is also one of the signs of His power, exalted is He. ﴿Indeed in that﴾, meaning what was mentioned, ﴿are signs for a people who use their reason﴾, meaning those who reflect.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 13, verse 5:**

﴿And if you are amazed﴾, O Muhammad, at the disbelievers' denial of you, ﴿then amazing is﴾ worthy of amazement ﴿their saying﴾, as they deny the resurrection, ﴿"When we are dust, shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ Because the One who is able to bring creation into being, and to create what came before it without any model, is able to restore them.

Regarding the two hamzahs (glottal stops, ء) in both places: there is *tahqiq* (pronouncing the hamzah in full, without softening) for both, and *tahqiq* of the first with *tashil* (softening the hamzah, pronouncing it between a hamzah and a vowel) of the second, with an alif inserted between them in both ways, and with the alif omitted. In one reading, the first is interrogative and the second is declarative; in another reading, it is the reverse of that.

It was revealed concerning their hastening of the punishment, mockingly: ﴿They ask you to hasten evil﴾ the punishment ﴿before good﴾ the mercy ﴿when exemplary punishments have already passed before them﴾. Al-Muthulat is the plural of al-mathulah (on the pattern of ath-thumrah), meaning the punishments (ʿuqubat) that befell their likes among the deniers. ﴿Will they not take heed from them?﴾ ﴿And indeed your Lord is Full of forgiveness for mankind despite﴾ (ʿala, meaning maʿa) ﴿their wrongdoing﴾, for otherwise He would not have left upon it (the earth) a single creature. ﴿And indeed your Lord is severe in punishment﴾ for whoever disobeys Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 7:

﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Why⁠—"﴾ (lawla, meaning) "hallā" (why not) ﴿is not a sign sent down upon him﴾ upon Muhammad ﴿from his Lord?﴾ such as the staff, the hand, and the she-camel. ﴿Indeed, you are only a warner﴾ one who frightens the disbelievers, and it is not upon you to bring the signs. ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾ a prophet who calls them to their Lord with what He gives him of signs, not with what they propose.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 8:

﴿Allah knows what every female carries﴾ whether male or female, one or more, and other than that. ﴿And what the wombs diminish﴾ decrease [in the period of gestation]. ﴿And what they increase﴾ from it. ﴿And everything with Him is in due measure﴾ with a decree and a limit it does not exceed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 13, verse 9:

﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: what is hidden and what is witnessed. ﴿The Great﴾: the magnificent. ﴿The Exalted﴾ (al-Mutaʿali) over His creation by dominance, read with a ya (المتعالي) and without it (المتعال).

﴿Equal to Him among you﴾ in His knowledge is ﴿the one who conceals speech and the one who speaks it aloud, and the one who is hidden﴾ concealed ﴿by the night﴾ by its darkness, ﴿and the one who goes forth﴾ openly visible by his going ﴿in his path﴾, that is, his way.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 11:

﴿For him﴾ (i.e., for the human being) ﴿are angels in succession﴾ (mu'aqqibat), angels who follow him one after another, ﴿before him and behind him﴾ (min bayni yadayhi): in front of him, ﴿and behind him﴾: behind him, ﴿who guard him﴾ (yahfazunahu) ﴿by the command of Allah﴾, meaning by His command, from the jinn and others. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change what is with a people﴾, i.e., He does not strip them of His blessing, ﴿until they change what is in themselves﴾, from the good condition by disobedience. ﴿And when Allah intends for a people an evil﴾, i.e., punishment, ﴿there is no averting it﴾, neither by the angels in succession nor by anything else. ﴿And they have not besides Him﴾, i.e., for those against whom Allah intends evil, ﴿any﴾ (min, here extra) ﴿protector﴾ (wali) ﴿who could ward it off from them.﴾

He it is Who shows you the lightning, as a fear (for travelers, of the thunderbolts) and as a hope (for the resident, of the rain), and He brings into being (yakhluq) the heavy clouds (al-sahab al-thiqal) laden with rain.

﴿And the thunder glorifies [Him] with His praise﴾: it is an angel appointed over the clouds, driving them while glorifying [Allah] with His praise. That is, it says, "Glory be to Allah and with His praise." ﴿And﴾ ﴿the angels [glorify Him] out of fear of Him﴾, that is, Allah. ﴿And He sends the thunderbolts﴾, which are fire that comes out of the clouds, ﴿and strikes with them whom He wills﴾, so that it burns him. It was revealed concerning a man whom the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for, inviting him [to Islam]. He said, "Who is the Messenger of Allah, and what is Allah? Is He of gold, or of silver, or of copper?" So a thunderbolt struck him and took away the top of his skull. ﴿While they﴾, that is, the unbelievers, ﴿dispute﴾, that is, argue with the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿about Allah. And He is severe in might﴾, meaning in strength, or in seizing [the wrongdoers].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 14:

﴿To Him is the true call﴾, i.e., His word, which is ﴿there is no god but Allah﴾. ﴿And those they call upon﴾ (with ya and ta' both read) ﴿besides Him﴾, i.e., other than Him, and they are the idols, ﴿do not respond to them with anything﴾ of what they ask for ﴿except﴾ a response ﴿like that of one who stretches out his hands toward the water﴾ at the edge of the well, calling to it, ﴿that it may reach his mouth﴾ by its rising up from the well to him, ﴿but it will never reach his mouth﴾, i.e., never, so likewise they will not respond to them. ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is not but in error﴾, i.e., their worship of the idols, or the reality of supplication is in error, ﴿error﴾ meaning loss.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 13, verse 15:

﴿And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly⁠ ﴾ like the believers, ﴿and unwillingly﴾ like the hypocrites, and those compelled by the sword. ﴿And﴾ their shadows prostrate ﴿in the mornings﴾ the early hours ﴿and the evenings﴾ the afternoons.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 16:

﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, to your people: ﴿"Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?" Say: "Allah."﴾ If they do not say it, there is no other answer. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"Have you then taken, besides Him, protectors (awliya', i.e., idols) that you worship, which have no power to benefit or harm themselves?"﴾ And you have abandoned the One who owns both? (This is an interrogative of rebuke.) ﴿Say: "Are the blind and the seeing alike?"﴾ (That is, the disbeliever and the believer.) ﴿Or are the darknesses (that is, disbelief) and the light (that is, faith) alike?﴾ No. ﴿Or have they set up for Allah partners who created as He creates, so that the creation (i.e., the creation of the partners) became confused to them with the creation of Allah?﴾ (This is an interrogative of denial: that is, the matter is not so, and none deserves worship except the Creator.) ﴿Upon them﴾ (so they believed that their worship was deserved because of their creating?). ﴿Say: "Allah is the Creator of all things,"﴾ with no partner in that, and therefore no partner in worship. ﴿And He is the One, the Subduer﴾ over His servants.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 17:

Then He struck a parable for the truth and the falsehood, saying: ﴿He sends down﴾ (God, exalted is He) ﴿from the sky water﴾ (rain), ﴿so the valleys flow according to their measure﴾ (according to the amount they can hold), ﴿and the torrent carries a foam rising﴾ (high) above it, which is what is on its surface of filth and the like. ﴿And from that which they kindle﴾ (with the tā' and the yā', both readings) ﴿upon it in the fire﴾ (from the substances of the earth, such as gold, silver and copper), ﴿seeking﴾ (desiring) ﴿ornament﴾ (adornment) ﴿or goods﴾ (things benefited from, such as vessels) when they are melted, ﴿there is a foam like it﴾ (i.e., like the foam of the torrent), and it is its dross which the bellows expel. ﴿Thus﴾ (the aforementioned) ﴿God strikes the truth and the falsehood﴾ (i.e., their parable). ﴿As for the foam﴾ (of the torrent and that which is kindled upon it of the substances), ﴿it passes away as scum﴾ (falsehood, cast off). ﴿But as for that which benefits people﴾ (of the water and the substances), ﴿it remains﴾ (abides) ﴿in the earth﴾ (for a time). Likewise falsehood vanishes and perishes, even if it rises above the truth at some times, while the truth is firm and enduring. ﴿Thus﴾ (the aforementioned) ﴿God strikes﴾ (makes clear) .

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 18:

﴿For those who respond to their Lord﴾ they responded to Him with obedience, ﴿the best [reward]﴾ Paradise. ﴿And those who do not respond to Him﴾ and they are the disbelievers, ﴿even if they had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would surely offer it as ransom﴾ from the punishment, ﴿those will have the terrible reckoning﴾ and it is the taking to account for everything they did, not one part of it being forgiven, ﴿and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ the bed, it is.

It was revealed concerning Hamza and Abu Jahl: ﴿Is he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth﴾ and so believes in it, ﴿like one who is blind?﴾ — one who does not know it and does not believe in it. ﴿Only those of understanding remember﴾ — they take heed — ﴿the people of intellect﴾, the possessors of minds.

Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah (the covenant taken from them while they were in the realm of atoms (ʿalam al-dharr), or any covenant) and do not break the pledge (by abandoning faith or the obligations).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 21:

﴿And those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾ of faith and the ties of kinship and other things. ﴿And they fear their Lord﴾ i.e., His threat. ﴿And they dread an evil reckoning﴾. The like of it has already been mentioned.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 13, verse 22:

﴿And those who are patient﴾ in obedience and in affliction, and abstain from disobedience, ﴿seeking﴾ (seeking) ﴿the countenance of their Lord﴾ alone, not any of the worldly goods, ﴿and establish the prayer, and spend﴾ in obedience ﴿of what We have provided them, secretly and openly, and repel﴾ (they repel) ﴿with good the evil﴾ such as repelling ignorance with forbearance and harm with patience. ﴿For those, there is the good outcome of the abode﴾ i.e., the praiseworthy consequence in the Hereafter, which is:

Gardens of Eden (ʿAdn) [where they will] reside; they will enter them, [along with] those who were righteous (ṣalaḥa) among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring, [i.e., those who] believed (āmana), even if they did not act like them, [and] they will be in their ranks as an honour for them. ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate﴾ of the gates of Paradise, or of its palaces, upon their first entry, to congratulate them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 24:

﴿They say, "Peace be upon you."﴾ This is the reward ﴿for what you patiently endured﴾, by your patience in the world. ﴿How excellent is the final abode﴾, your final outcome.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 25:

﴿And those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined and cause corruption on the earth﴾ by disbelief and sins, ﴿those will have the curse﴾ the distance from the mercy of Allah, ﴿and they will have the evil abode﴾ the evil consequence in the Hereafter, which is Jahannam (Hell).

Allah extends provision (yabsut al-rizq) to whomever He wills and restricts it (yaqdir). He widens it (yuwassi'uhu) for whomever He wills and narrows it (yudayyiquhu) for whomever He wills.

"And they rejoice" — i.e., the people of Makkah rejoice with exultation (farah batar) "in the life of this world" — i.e., in what they have attained therein. "Yet the life of this world, in comparison to the Hereafter, is nothing but a fleeting enjoyment" — a small thing that is enjoyed and then passes away.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 27:

﴿And those who disbelieve say﴾ from among the people of Makkah, ﴿"Why is it not⁠ [⁠lawla⁠]⁠ (lawla: "why not", "would that") sent down upon him⁠"⁠ upon Muhammad, ﴿a sign from his Lord﴾ like the staff, the hand and the she-camel. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"Indeed Allah leaves astray whom He wills"⁠ — leaving him astray, so the signs avail them nothing — ﴿and guides﴾ directs ﴿to Him﴾ to His religion ﴿whoever turns back﴾ returns ﴿to Him.﴾ (man is substituted for the preceding man).

﴿Those who believe and whose hearts find rest﴾ settle [تَسْكُنُ] ﴿in the remembrance of Allah﴾, i.e., His promise. ﴿Surely, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest﴾, i.e., the hearts of the believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 29:

﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is ﴿Tuba﴾, a verbal noun (masdar) from "al-tayyib" (goodness), or a tree in Paradise, under whose shade a rider travels a hundred years without crossing it. ﴿For them is good, and a good return﴾, i.e., a place of return.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 30:

﴿Thus⁠﴾ as We sent the prophets before you, ﴿We have sent you to a community, before which communities have passed away, so that you may recite⁠﴾ read ﴿to them that which We have revealed to you⁠﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful⁠﴾ when they were commanded to prostrate to Him, they said: "And what is the Most Merciful?" ﴿Say⁠﴾ to them, O Muhammad,

Revealed when they said to him: "If you are a prophet, then move the mountains of Makkah away from us, make for us rivers and springs in it so that we may plant and sow, and raise for us our forefathers who have died, so that they may speak to us that you are a prophet." ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains were moved﴾ from their places, ﴿or the earth were split﴾ cleft ﴿by it, or the dead were made to speak﴾ by being brought back to life, ﴿[it would not be other than this]⁠—⁠﴾ when they believed. ﴿Rather, the command belongs entirely to Allah﴾, not to anyone else; so none believes except whom He wills to believe, apart from others. Even if they were given what they proposed... It was revealed when the Companions wished to display what they had proposed, out of hope for their faith. ﴿Have not those who believe despaired﴾ known ﴿that﴾ here it is the light (mukhaffafah) form, meaning that ﴿if Allah willed, He would have guided all mankind﴾ to faith without a sign. ﴿And those who disbelieve will never cease to be struck﴾ among the people of Makkah ﴿for what they have done﴾ by their deeds, namely their disbelief, ﴿by a calamity﴾ a disaster that strikes them with various kinds of trials: killing, captivity, war and drought. ﴿Or it will settle﴾ O Muhammad, with your army ﴿near their homes﴾ Makkah ﴿until the promise of Allah comes﴾ with victory over them. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise﴾. And it did settle at Hudaybiyah, until the conquest of Makkah came.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 32:

﴿And indeed, messengers before you were mocked﴾, just as you are mocked. This is a consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿Then I granted respite﴾, i.e., I gave time, ﴿to those who disbelieved; then I seized them﴾ with punishment. ﴿So how was My punishment﴾, i.e., it was fittingly applied. Likewise I shall deal with those who mock you.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 13, verse 33:

﴿Is then He who stands over every soul, [watching] what it has earned,﴾ [i.e., the watcher, Allah, over every soul concerning what it has done of good and evil, and that is Allah, ﴿like those who have no such [power]?﴾ i.e., the idols; there is no proof for this] ﴿Yet they ascribe to Allah partners.﴾ ﴿Say, "Name them!"﴾ Who are they? ﴿Or is it that you inform Him of something He does not know in the earth?﴾ [Or rather, do you inform Allah of a partner ﴿He does not know﴾ of, i.e., there is no partner, since if there were one, He, exalted be He above that, would know of it. This is an interrogative of denial.] ﴿Or is it [merely] an outward saying?﴾ [Or rather, do you name them partners by a false assumption that has no reality within?] ﴿Rather, the plotting of those who disbelieved has been made attractive to them,﴾ [their disbelief has been made attractive to them] ﴿and they have been barred from the way.﴾ [the path of guidance]

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah 13 (ar-Ra'd), verse 34:

﴿Theirs is a punishment in the life of this world﴾ by being killed and taken captive, ﴿but the punishment of the Hereafter is harder﴾, more severe than it, ﴿and they will have no protector from Allah﴾, i.e., from His punishment, ﴿any defender﴾, a preventer.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 35:

﴿Mathal﴾ (the description/parable) of ﴿al-Jannah allati wu'ida al-muttaqun﴾ (the Garden that the God-fearing have been promised) is a subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is omitted, meaning: "in what is recited to you." ﴿Its fruit﴾ (ukuluha) is what is eaten therein; ﴿perpetual﴾ (da'im) that does not perish; ﴿and its shade﴾ (wa-zilluha) is perpetual, not abrogated (lā tansakhuhu) by a sun, because there is no sun in it. ﴿That﴾ (tilka), i.e., the Garden, is ﴿the final outcome (uqba)﴾ (aqibah) of ﴿those who have guarded themselves﴾ (alladhina ittaqaw) against shirk (ash-shirk).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 36:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book﴾ such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and others among the believing Jews, ﴿rejoice at what has been sent down to you﴾ because it agrees with what they have, ﴿and among the factions﴾ those who united against you in enmity from among the polytheists and the Jews ﴿are those who deny part of it﴾ such as the mention of the All-Merciful and what is other than the stories. ﴿Say: "I have only been commanded﴾ regarding what has been sent down to me ﴿to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him. To Him I call, and to Him is my return﴾ my place of return.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 37:

﴿And thus﴾ the revelation, ﴿We sent it down﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿as a judgment (ḥukman) in Arabic﴾, in the language of the Arabs, by which you judge between the people. ﴿And if you were to follow their desires﴾, i.e., the disbelievers', in what they call you to of their religion, supposing it, ﴿after the knowledge has come to you﴾ of monotheism, ﴿you would have from Allah no protector (walī) nor any defender (wāqin)﴾, i.e., nothing to prevent His punishment. Here "min" in ﴿min Allāh min﴾ is extra (zāʾida), and walī means helper (nāṣir), while wāqin means one who wards off (māniʿ) from His punishment.

It was revealed when they reproached him for having many wives: ﴿And We had certainly sent messengers before you and made for them wives and offspring﴾ (children), and you are like them. ﴿And it was not for a messenger﴾ among them ﴿to bring a sign except by permission of Allah﴾, because they are servants, owned and managed. ﴿For every term there is a Book﴾ (a period), a decree written in it, specifying its determined limit.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 39:

﴿Allah effaces﴾ from it ﴿what He wills, and confirms﴾ — with light and heavy pronunciation — in it ﴿what He wills⌋ of the rulings and other things. ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, its origin, which nothing in it changes, and it is what He wrote in eternity (al-azal).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 13, verse 40:

﴿Whether﴾ (wa-immā): here the nūn of the conditional particle in (in) is assimilated into the extra (zā'ida) mā. ﴿We show you some of﴾ what ﴿We promise them﴾ of punishment, ﴿in your lifetime,﴾ and the response of the condition is omitted, meaning: then that is (what will happen). ﴿Or We take you back to Us﴾ before their punishment, ﴿then upon you is only the conveying﴾ (al-balāgh), meaning: upon you is nothing but the conveying (al-tablīgh) ﴿and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ when they come back to Us, so We will requite them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 41:

﴿Do they not see﴾ i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿that We come to the land﴾ intending their land, ﴿reducing it from its borders﴾ by conquest, granted to the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿And Allah judges﴾ over His creation as He wills, ﴿there is none to repel His judgment﴾, i.e., none to turn it back.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 42:

﴿And those before them had already plotted,﴾ of the nations against their prophets, just as they have plotted against you. ﴿But to Allah belongs all planning.﴾ Their plotting is not like His plotting, because He ﴿knows what every soul earns,﴾ so He prepares for it its recompense; and this is the whole of planning, for He comes upon them from where they do not perceive. ﴿And the disbelievers will know﴾ (the word refers to the category, and in another reading, "the disbelievers") ﴿to whom will belong the good outcome of the Home,﴾ meaning the praiseworthy end in the Hereafter: is it for them, or for the Prophet ﷺ and his companions?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 13, verse 43:

﴿And those who disbelieve say﴾ to you, ﴿"You are not a messenger."﴾ Say ﴿"Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you"﴾ concerning my truthfulness, ﴿and [sufficient is] whoever has knowledge of the Book﴾ from the believers among the Jews and the Christians.
